page.layout: Two medallion portraits with legends across the top of the page, centred over the text; below them one column of text in two paragraphs, the first beginning FRANCISCVS and the second beginning GALEATIVS. Running head at top right with page number.

main_text.p: FRANCISCVS Sforza, Sforzæ à Cutiniola filius, Philippi Marię Vicecomitis gener, ab eodē adoptatus est, &angue[?], insigni familiæ donatus, anno salutis 1430. socero defuncto, proximo statim anno, ob singularem virtutem Mediolani principatum adeptus est. Hic Sforzæ cognomen à Sforza patre bellicofo traxit: qui humilis & abiectus, cum se militiæ tradidiffer, per vim ab aliis quicquid cuperet extorquebat, sicque Sforzæ cognomen affecutus, vt proprium nomen semper postea habuit, & ad posteros cognomen trānsmisit. Hic per cunctos gradus, ad summum militiæ culmen conscendit. Contra Eugenium Papam, contra Florentinos, Venetos, Mediolanenses, non semel victor, Guelforum, ac Gibellinorum nomen ferè è medio tulit, Italiæ vniuersæ propemodum factus terror. Composita cum Venetis pace, multæ Italiæ ciuitates eius exēpla secutæ, arma depofuere. Intus forisque pacatis omnibus, à fundamentis denuò erexit castrū Mediolani, quod Iouis dicitur, à populo antea dirutum. Magnum illud hospitale, ægrotis recipiendis, ædificauit, quod regali censu ditauit, opus in orbe rarum. Vt diui Ambr. têplum erigeret, multum auri expendit. Tandem verò hic tantus vir, adeò libidine exarsit, vt adolescentum flagitia superarit. rexit an. 16. obiit, sex filiis duabúsque filiabus relictis, anno salutis 1466. Vide Supplem.lib.15. & Archie. Antonium.

GALEATIVS Maria, Francisco Sforzæ patri defuncto, statim in Mediolani principatu succedit, pulsa matre quæ rem cum eo administrabat: multis hic se inquinauit flagitiis: quamobrem adulteriis, homicidiis, incestibus, sacrilegiisque pollutus anno administrationis 9. liberis 4. relictis, in æde Diui Stephani vulneribus est confossus. Vide Supplem.Chron.

page.notes: Medallion legends are engraved, not set type; the two lines above are read from the curved inscriptions and are doubtful, especially the ends of each line (DVX, MAVI, CŌ. D. MILIS). The "&angue" reading in the first paragraph is doubtful. Faint show-through of the reverse page is visible below the text and was left out. A small mark "1" stands at the bottom centre; it is not clearly a gathering signature and was left out. The text has no catchword.
